facts.fact: The Ministry's completed-projects page says the Tanzania National e-Procurement System (TANePS) was completed and put into use under the RCIP project, which ended December 2017.

TZA.note: A cyber security strategy is said to be prepared, not adopted; no national body named.

facts.fact: The Ministry says the government enacted the Cyber Crime Act, 2015 under the RCIP project.

TZA.note: Data centres named, with no statement that either rents space or computing to others.

facts.fact: The Ministry says a draft Personal Data Protection Bill had been prepared by the end of the RCIP project in December 2017.

TZA.note: Government Data Centre is said to be built and working, with no statement that state data or systems are hosted there.

facts.fact: The Ministry says the government enacted the Electronic Transaction Act, 2015 under the RCIP project.
The Ministry says the National ICT Backbone, 7,910 km, links the headquarters of 25 mainland regions and 42 of 139 districts, built in three phases from 2009 to 2016.
The Ministry says that in phase I (2009-2010) the national backbone was also connected to the SEACOM and EASSy submarine cables.
The Ministry says the government completed eGovernment Standards and Guidelines so that systems of government bodies are secure, standard and able to exchange information.
The Ministry says the e-Government Agency (eGA) built the e-Office system, which government institutions use for daily work.

The Ministry says a government-funded project connected ten council offices (Katesh, Uvinza, Wanging'ombe, Urambo, Kaliua, Mbulu, Monduli, Sikonge, Simanjiro and Kiteto) to the national backbone, June 2018 to April 2019.
The Ministry names ten councils connected to the national backbone in the 2018-2019 project, giving no total of councils.
